'''Stuart Stephen Papworth Parkin''' (born 9 December 1955<ref name="leopoldina-cv">{{cite web|title=Curriculum Vitae Professor Dr. Stuart Parkin|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Parkin_Stuart_EN.pdf|publisher=German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|access-date=12 November 2023|archive-date=29 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211129124116/https://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Parkin_Stuart_EN.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>) is an [[experimental physicist]], Managing Director at the [[Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics]] in [[Halle (Saale)|Halle]] and an [[Alexander von Humboldt Professorship|Alexander von Humboldt Professor]] at the Institute of Physics of the [[Martin-Luther-University Halle-Wittenberg]].<ref name="mpg-cv">{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Stuart Parkin: Curriculum Vitae |url=https://www.mpg.de/8184715/microstructure-physics-parkin |publisher=Max-Planck-Gesellschaft |access-date=12 October 2023}}</ref>

He is a pioneer in the science and application of [[spintronic]] materials, and has made discoveries into the behaviour of thin-film magnetic structures that were critical in enabling recent increases in the data density and capacity of computer hard-disk drives. For these discoveries, he was awarded the 2014 [[Millennium Technology Prize]].<ref name="MTPrize_TAF">{{cite web|title=Physicist Stuart Parkin wins 2014 Millennium Technology Prize for opening big data era|url=http://taf.fi/en/2014/04/09/physicist-stuart-parkin-wins-2014-millennium-technology-prize-for-opening-big-data-era/|publisher=Technology Academy Finland|accessdate=9 April 2014|archive-date=2 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140902141329/http://taf.fi/en/2014/04/09/physicist-stuart-parkin-wins-2014-millennium-technology-prize-for-opening-big-data-era/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="MTPrize_theguardian">{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2014/apr/09/stuart-parkin-millennium-technology-prize-cloud-computing|title=Stuart Parkin awarded prestigious Millennium Technology Prize|last=Davis|first=Nicola|work=The Guardian|date=9 April 2014|accessdate=9 April 2014|archive-date=10 April 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140410220019/http://www.theguardian.com/technology/2014/apr/09/stuart-parkin-millennium-technology-prize-cloud-computing|url-status=live}}</ref> 

Before his current position, Parkin was an [[IBM Fellow]] and manager of the magnetoelectronics group at the [[IBM]] [[Almaden Research Center]] in San Jose, California. He was also a consulting professor in the department of applied physics at [[Stanford University]] and director of the IBM-Stanford Spintronic Science and Applications Center, which was formed in 2004.<ref>[http://www.almaden.ibm.com/spinaps/ IBM-Stanford Spintronic Science and Applications Center] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080412024538/http://www.almaden.ibm.com/spinaps/ |date=12 April 2008 }}</ref>

==Education and early life==
A native of [[Watford]], England,<ref name="wired-millennium">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.wired.co.uk/news/archive/2014-04/09/stuart-parkin-prize|title=Data storage pioneer wins €1m Millennium Technology Prize|last=Solon|first=Olivia|magazine=Wired|date=9 April 2014|access-date=9 April 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140411001332/http://www.wired.co.uk/news/archive/2014-04/09/stuart-parkin-prize|archive-date=11 April 2014|df=dmy-all}}</ref> Parkin received his B.A. (1977) and was elected a research fellow (1979) at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]], England, and was awarded his PhD (1980) at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]], also in Cambridge. He joined IBM in 1982 as a World Trade Post-doctoral Fellow, becoming a permanent member of the staff the following year. In 1999 he was named an IBM Fellow, IBM's highest technical honour.<ref name="humboldt-foundation">{{cite web|url=http://www.humboldt-foundation.de/web/ahp-2014-en.html|title=Alexander von Humboldt Professorship – The Award Winners 2014|publisher=Alexander von Humboldt-Foundation|accessdate=9 April 2014|archive-date=3 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140503193843/http://www.humboldt-foundation.de/web/ahp-2014-en.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Research and career==
In 2007 Parkin was named a distinguished visiting professor at the [[National University of Singapore]], a visiting chair professor at the [[National Taiwan University]], and an honorary visiting professor at [[University College London]].  In 2008, he was elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www8.nationalacademies.org/onpinews/newsitem.aspx?RecordID=04292008 |title=Election to U.S. National Academy of Sciences |access-date=27 May 2008 |archive-date=1 May 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080501085352/http://www8.nationalacademies.org/onpinews/newsitem.aspx?RecordID=04292008 |url-status=live }}</ref> The Materials Research Network Dresden granted him the Dresden Barkhausen Award in 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mfd-dresden.com/en/events/barkhausen-award/awardees.html|title=List of the Barkhausen Awardees|publisher=Materials Research Network Dresden|access-date=9 April 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140413124839/http://www.mfd-dresden.com/en/events/barkhausen-award/awardees.html|archive-date=13 April 2014|df=dmy-all}}</ref> Parkin has been awarded honorary doctorates by the [[RWTH Aachen|University of Aachen]], Germany in 2007<ref>{{cite web |title=Honorary Degree Aachen |url=https://www.fb1.rwth-aachen.de/cms/mathematik-naturwissenschaften/die-fakultaet/auszeichnungen-und-ehrendoktoren/~laas/ehrendoktoren/?lidx=1 |website=Honorary Degrees Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences |publisher=RWTH Aachen |access-date=6 March 2026}}</ref>, the [[Eindhoven University of Technology]], The Netherlands in 2008<ref>{{cite web |title=Honorary Degree Eindhoven |url=https://www.tue.nl/en/news/news-overview/09-04-2014-millennium-technology-prize-for-tue-distinguished-professor |website=Millennium Technology Prize for TU/e distinguished professor |publisher=Eindhoven University of Technology |access-date=6 March 2026}}</ref>, the [[University of Regensburg|University of Regensburg]], Germany in 2011<ref>{{cite web |title=Honorary Degree Regensburg |url=https://portal.uni-regensburg.de/1695/1/jahresbericht-2011.pdf |website=Annual Report 2011 |publisher=University of Regensburg |access-date=6 March 2026}}</ref> and the [[University of Kaiserslautern|University of Kaiserslautern]], Germany in 2013<ref>{{cite web |title=Honorary Degree Kaiserslautern |url=https://optimas.uni-kl.de/en/news/news/news/honorary-doctorate-of-the-university-of-kaiserslautern-for-pioneer-of-modern-computer-technology |website=Honorary Doctorate of the University of Kaiserslautern for pioneer of modern Computer Technology |publisher=University of Kaiserslautern |access-date=6 March 2026}}</ref>.

In 1989 Stuart Parkin discovered the phenomenon of oscillatory interlayer coupling in magnetic multilayers, by which magnetic layers are magnetically coupled via an intervening non-magnetic metallic spacer layer.  Parkin found that the sign of the exchange coupling oscillates from ferromagnetic to antiferromagnetic with an oscillation period of just a few atomic layers. Remarkably, Parkin discovered this phenomenon in thin film magnetic heterostructures that he prepared in a simple home-made sputtering system. Parkin, moreover, showed that this phenomenon is displayed by almost all metallic transition elements. In what is often referred to as "Parkin's Periodic Table", Parkin showed that the strength of this oscillatory interlayer exchange interaction varied systematically across the Periodic Table of the elements.  Parkin made numerous other fundamental discoveries which continued the development of the field of "spintronics" of which he is recognised as a prolific scientist.

Later Parkin improved magnetic tunnelling junctions, a device invented in the 1970s by Julliere, and revolutionized by Jagadeesh Moodera of MIT. This element can create a high performance magnetic random access memory in 1995.<ref name="wired-millennium"/> [[Magnetoresistive RAM|Magnetoresistive random-access memory]] (MRAM) promises unique attributes of high speed, high density and non-volatility. The development by Parkin in 2001 of giant tunnelling magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions using highly textured MgO tunnel barriers has made MRAM even more promising. IBM developed the first MRAM prototype in 1999 and is currently developing a 16 Mbit chip.

Parkin's research interests include organic superconductors, high-temperature superconductors, and, most recently, magnetic thin film structures and spintronic materials and devices for advanced sensor, memory, and logic applications. Most recently, Parkin has proposed and is working on a novel storage class memory device, The Magnetic [[Racetrack memory]], which could replace both hard disk drives and many forms of conventional solid state memory.<ref name="ibm-research-bio">{{cite web|url=http://researcher.watson.ibm.com/researcher/view.php?person=us-stuart.parkin|title=Stuart S.P. Parkin|publisher=IBM Research|accessdate=9 April 2014|archive-date=20 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140820025147/http://researcher.watson.ibm.com/researcher/view.php?person=us-stuart.parkin}}</ref><ref name="bbc-millennium">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-26929250|title=Hard disk pioneer Stuart Parkin wins Millennium Prize|publisher=BBC News|date=9 April 2014|accessdate=9 April 2014|archive-date=9 April 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140409132635/http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-26929250|url-status=live}}</ref> His research interests also include spin transistors and spin-logic devices that may enable a new generation of low-power electronics.

Parkin has received two [[ERC Advanced Grant]]s: The first was awarded in 2014 and focused on spin-orbitronics for electronic technologies ("SORBET"). The second was awarded in 2022, focusing on the interplay between chirality, spin textures and superconductivity at manufactured interfaces ("SUPERMINT").<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Stuart Parkin wins his second ERC Advanced Grant |url=https://www.mpi-halle.mpg.de/stuart-parkin-second-erc-grant |website=Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics |access-date=12 November 2023 |language=en}}</ref>

Parkin has authored over 670 papers and has more than 123 issued patents.<ref name="mpg-cv"/> [[Clarivate]] has named Parkin a "Highly Cited Researcher in the field of Physics" for the years 2018–2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Stuart Parkin |url=https://www.webofscience.com/wos/author/record/D-2521-2012 |website=Web of Science |access-date=12 November 2023}}</ref> He is also the chief editor of Spin, one of [[World Scientific]]'s newest journals, which publishes articles in spin electronics.<ref name="SPIN-chief-editor">{{cite web|url=http://www.worldscientific.com/page/spin/editorial-board|title=Stuart Parkin, Chief Editor of Spin|publisher=World Scientific|accessdate=24 April 2014|archive-date=29 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211129122318/https://www.worldscientific.com/page/spin/editorial-board|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Parkin is married to the chemist [[Claudia Felser]], who herself is director of the [[Max Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids]] in [[Dresden]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Smith |first=Kerri |date=1 June 2014 |title=Love in the lab: Close collaborators |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=510 |issue=7506 |pages=458–460 |doi=10.1038/510458a |pmid=24965634 |bibcode=2014Natur.510..458S |s2cid=4399741 |issn=1476-4687|doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Awards==
Parkin is the recipient of numerous honours, including the Gutenberg Research Award (2008), a [[Humboldt Prize|Humboldt Research Award]] (2004), the 1999–2000 [[American Institute of Physics]] Prize for Industrial Applications of Physics,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aip.org/industry/prize/parkin|title=Stuart Parkin|date=14 January 2014|publisher=American Institute of Physics|accessdate=9 April 2014|archive-date=13 April 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140413124924/http://www.aip.org/industry/prize/parkin|url-status=live}}</ref> the [[European Physical Society]]'s [[Europhysics Prize]] (1997), the American Physical Society's International New Materials Prize (1994), the MRS Outstanding Young Investigator Award (1991) and the Charles Vernon Boys Prize from the Institute of Physics, London (1991). In 2001, he was named the first "Innovator of the Year" by ''R&D Magazine'' and in October 2007 was received the "No Boundaries" Award for Innovation from ''[[The Economist]]''. The [[IEEE Daniel E. Noble Award]] for Emerging Technologies was awarded to Parkin in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IEEE Lotfi A. Zadeh Award for Emerging Technologies |url=https://corporate-awards.ieee.org/award/ieee-lofti-zadeh-award/ |access-date=21 August 2026}}</ref> In 2009, Parkin was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences|Fellow of the American Academy of Art and Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-08-10 |title=Stuart Stephen Papworth Parkin {{!}} American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/stuart-stephen-papworth-parkin |access-date=2026-08-21 |website=www.amacad.org |language=en}}</ref> and received the {{ill|IUPAP Magnetism Award and Néel Medal|de}} of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=C9: Awards |url=https://iupap.org/who-we-are/internal-organization/commissions/c9-magnetism/c9-awards/ |website=IUPAP: The International Union of Pure and Applied Physics |access-date=12 November 2023 |date=10 March 2021}}</ref> In 2012, Parkin was awarded the [[Von Hippel Award]] of the [[Materials Research Society]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Materials Research Society |url=https://www.mrs.org/careers-advancement/awards/fall-awards/von-hippel-award |website=MRS Awards: Von Hippel Award |access-date=12 November 2023}}</ref> as well as the [[David Adler Lectureship Award|David Adler Lectureship Award in the Field of Materials Physics]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=David Adler Lectureship Award in the Field of Materials Physics |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/award/david-adler-lectureship-award |access-date=2026-08-21 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>. In April 2014, Parkin was awarded the [[Millennium Technology Prize]] for his work on spintronic materials, "leading to a prodigious growth in the capacity to store digital information".<ref name="MTPrize_TAF"/><ref name="MTPrize_theguardian"/> In 2021 he received the [[King Faisal Prize]] in Science.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://kingfaisalprize.org/ |title=King Faisal Prize 2021 |access-date=10 February 2021 |archive-date=9 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181209171102/http://kingfaisalprize.org/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2023, Parkin was named a [[Clarivate Citation Laureates|Clarivate Citation Laureate]] in Physics, an award given out to scientists considered likely to receive a [[Nobel Prize]] in the future.<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Stuart Parkin recognized as Clarivate Citation Laureate |url=https://www.mpi-halle.mpg.de/stuart-parkin-citation-laureate |website=Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics |access-date=13 November 2023 |language=en}}</ref> Parkin received the 2024 [[List of American Physical Society prizes and awards#APS Medal for Exceptional Achievement in Research|APS Medal for Exceptional Achievement in Research]] for contributions to spintronics and data storage.<ref>{{cite web |title=APS Medal for Exceptional Achievement in Research |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/prize/aps-medal |website=www.aps.org |access-date=29 January 2025 |language=en}}</ref> Parkin was awarded the [[Charles Stark Draper Prize]] in 2024 for his "inventions in the field of spintronics".<ref>{{cite web |title='Spintronics' Pioneer Receives Draper Prize, Engineering's Top Honor |url=https://www.draper.com/press-release/spintronics-pioneer-receives-draper-prize-engineerings-top-honor |website=www.draper.com |access-date=15 January 2024 |language=en |date=3 January 2024}}</ref>

==Memberships==
Parkin is a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]], the [[American Physical Society]], the Materials Research Society, the Institute of Physics (London), the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]], the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], and the Gutenberg Research College (GRC).

In 2008, Parkin was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Stuart S. P. Parkin |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/stuart-s-p-parkin-l4fg0z/ |website=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=12 November 2023}}</ref> In 2009, he was elected into the [[National Academy of Engineering]] for contributions to development of spin-engineered magnetic heterostructures for magnetic sensors and memory devices.<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Stuart S. P. Parkin |url=https://www.nae.edu/30917/Prof-Dr-Stuart-S-P-Parkin |website=NAE Website |access-date=12 November 2023 |language=en}}</ref> In 2012, he was elected into [[The World Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Parkin, Stuart Stephen Papworth |url=https://twas.org/directory/parkin-stuart-stephen-papworth |website=The World Academy of Sciences (TWAS) |language=en |access-date=12 November 2023}}</ref> The same year, he received an Honorary fellowship of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. S S P Parkin |url=https://fellows.ias.ac.in/profile/v/FH2012034 |website=Indian Academy of Sciences, Bengaluru: Fellows' portal |access-date=12 November 2023}}</ref> In 2015, he became a member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Stuart Parkin|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/stuart-parkin/|publisher=German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|access-date=26 May 2021|archive-date=26 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526194322/https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/stuart-parkin/|url-status=live}}</ref> Since March 2016, Parkin is an International Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]], Scotland's national academy of science and letters.<ref>{{cite web|title=Professor Stuart Parkin IntFRSE|url=https://rse.org.uk/fellowship/fellow/professor-stuart-parkin-14781/ |website=Royal Society of Edinburgh |access-date=29 January 2025 |language=en}}</ref> In 2019, he became a fellow of the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Stuart Parkin |url=https://raeng.org.uk/about-us/fellowship/new-fellows-2019/stuart-parkin |website=Royal Academy of Engineering |access-date=12 November 2023 |language=en}}</ref>
